```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5, dpi = 150)
library(tidyverse)

# --- arm palette -------------------------------------------------------------
# Three categorical series, fixed order, never cycled. Validated against the
# six colour checks (lightness band, chroma floor, CVD adjacent dE, normal-
# vision floor, contrast) in both light and dark surfaces before use.
ARM_LEVELS <- c("single-BROKEN", "single-FIXED", "multi")
ARM_PAL <- c("single-BROKEN" = "#0072B2",
             "single-FIXED"  = "#D55E00",
             "multi"         = "#009E73")

# Ordinal: MIMAG tiers are ranked, so one hue light -> dark, not categorical hues.
TIER_LEVELS <- c("HQ", "MQ", "LQ")
TIER_PAL <- c("HQ" = "#1b4f72", "MQ" = "#5499c7", "LQ" = "#aed6f1")

INK   <- "#1a1a19"   # primary text
MUTED <- "#6b6b68"   # secondary text / axes

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#e8e8e6", linewidth = 0.3),
      axis.text  = element_text(colour = MUTED),
      axis.title = element_text(colour = MUTED),
      plot.title = element_text(colour = INK, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = MUTED),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(colour = INK, face = "bold")
    )
)

tier_of <- function(compl, contam) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    compl >  90 & contam <  5 ~ "HQ",
    compl >= 50 & contam < 10 ~ "MQ",
    TRUE                      ~ "LQ"
  )
}
```

# What this compares

Three arms, same 22 samples, same assemblies, same binner builds.

| Arm | Depth information | MaxBin2 abundance |
|---|---|---|
| **single-BROKEN** | one sample | jgi table passed to `-abund` → contigLen read as abundance |
| **single-FIXED** *(baseline)* | one sample | correct 2-column file |
| **multi** | 22 samples | correct per-sample 2-column files via `-abund_list` |

`single-BROKEN` is reused unchanged from the original run and is shown as a
reference point only. **The valid comparison is single-FIXED vs multi**: it is
the only pair that differs in exactly one thing, the number of samples
contributing coverage. MaxBin2 supplies 18.6% of the DAS Tool bins across the
full 113-sample dataset, so leaving the abundance bug in the baseline would
have let the bug fix masquerade as a method effect.

```{r inputs}
subset <- read_tsv(params$subset_tsv, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(role = factor(role, levels = c("failure", "control", "depth_contrast")),
         stratum = if_else(subgenus == "Pyrobombus",
                           "within-subgenus", "cross-subgenus"))

inputs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~what,                   ~path,
  "checkm single-FIXED",   file.path(params$results, "checkm/checkm_qa_single_fixed.tsv"),
  "checkm multi",          file.path(params$results, "checkm/checkm_qa_multi.tsv"),
  "checkm single-BROKEN",  file.path(params$work_base, "05_binning/checkm_qa_ALL.tsv"),
  "gtdbtk new arms",       file.path(params$results, "gtdbtk/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv"),
  "gtdbtk single-BROKEN",  file.path(params$work_base, "08_gtdbtk/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv")
) %>% mutate(exists = file.exists(path))

knitr::kable(inputs, caption = "Inputs")
stopifnot("Some inputs are missing — see the table above" = all(inputs$exists))
```

# 1. DAS Tool bins per sample

```{r bins}
# Per-binner provenance comes from DAS Tool's own summary table: its `bin_set`
# column is authoritative, unlike guessing from bin names.
read_dastool <- function(arm, dir_fun) {
  subset$sample %>%
    set_names() %>%
    map(function(s) {
      f <- dir_fun(s)
      if (!file.exists(f)) return(tibble(bin = character(), bin_set = character()))
      read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% select(bin, bin_set)
    }) %>%
    bind_rows(.id = "sample") %>%
    mutate(arm = arm)
}

dastool <- bind_rows(
  read_dastool("single-BROKEN", function(s)
    file.path(params$work_base, "05_binning", s, "DASTool",
              paste0(s, "_DASTool_DASTool_summary.tsv"))),
  read_dastool("single-FIXED", function(s)
    file.path(params$results, "single_fixed", s, "DASTool",
              paste0(s, "_DASTool_DASTool_summary.tsv"))),
  read_dastool("multi", function(s)
    file.path(params$results, "multi", s, "DASTool",
              paste0(s, "_DASTool_DASTool_summary.tsv")))
) %>% mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = ARM_LEVELS))

bins_per_sample <- subset %>%
  select(sample, species, subgenus, role, stratum) %>%
  crossing(arm = factor(ARM_LEVELS, levels = ARM_LEVELS)) %>%
  left_join(count(dastool, sample, arm, name = "n_bins"), by = c("sample", "arm")) %>%
  mutate(n_bins = replace_na(n_bins, 0L))

bins_per_sample %>%
  group_by(arm) %>%
  summarise(total_bins = sum(n_bins),
            samples_with_zero = sum(n_bins == 0),
            median_bins = median(n_bins), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Bins per arm across the 22 subset samples")
```

```{r bins-plot, fig.height=7}
ord <- bins_per_sample %>% filter(arm == "multi") %>% arrange(role, n_bins) %>% pull(sample)

ggplot(bins_per_sample, aes(x = n_bins, y = factor(sample, levels = ord), colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = sample), colour = "#d5d5d2", linewidth = 2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ARM_PAL, breaks = ARM_LEVELS) +
  facet_grid(role ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "DAS Tool bins per sample",
       subtitle = "Grey line joins the three arms for one sample; samples grouped by their role in the design",
       x = "bins", y = NULL)
```

# 2. MIMAG tiers (CheckM1)

All arms measured with the same CheckM1 install. `HQ` = >90% complete and
<5% contaminated; `MQ` = ≥50% and <10%; everything else `LQ`.

```{r checkm}
# The existing combined table has a header shifted by one column (5c prepends a
# SAMPLE column to the data rows but not to the header). Read it positionally.
read_broken_checkm <- function(f) {
  hdr <- read_lines(f, n_max = 1) %>% str_split("\t") %>% unlist()
  read_tsv(f, skip = 1, col_names = c("SAMPLE", hdr), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

qual <- bind_rows(
  read_broken_checkm(inputs$path[inputs$what == "checkm single-BROKEN"]) %>%
    transmute(arm = "single-BROKEN", sample = SAMPLE, bin = `Bin Id`,
              compl = Completeness, contam = Contamination) %>%
    semi_join(subset, by = "sample"),
  read_tsv(inputs$path[inputs$what == "checkm single-FIXED"], show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    transmute(arm = "single-FIXED", sample = SAMPLE, bin = BIN,
              compl = Completeness, contam = Contamination),
  read_tsv(inputs$path[inputs$what == "checkm multi"], show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    transmute(arm = "multi", sample = SAMPLE, bin = BIN,
              compl = Completeness, contam = Contamination)
) %>%
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = ARM_LEVELS),
         tier = factor(tier_of(compl, contam), levels = TIER_LEVELS))

qual %>% count(arm, tier) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = tier, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Bins by MIMAG tier")
```

```{r tiers-plot, fig.height=3.4}
ggplot(count(qual, arm, tier), aes(x = n, y = fct_rev(arm), fill = tier)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n > 0, n, "")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            colour = "white", size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = TIER_PAL, breaks = TIER_LEVELS) +
  labs(title = "MIMAG tiers per arm", subtitle = "CheckM1 on all three arms", x = "bins", y = NULL)
```

# 3. Per-binner contribution — the CONCOCT retention test

CONCOCT is **already the largest contributor** to the existing MAG set (86 of
183 bins dataset-wide, 59 of them high quality). The hypothesis is not that it
starts working, but that its **retention rate** improves: it currently produces
16–55 bins per sample of which DAS Tool keeps 0–2, because it was given a
single coverage column when it is designed to exploit covariance across many.

```{r binner}
binner <- dastool %>% semi_join(subset, by = "sample") %>% count(arm, bin_set)

binner %>% pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "DAS Tool bins by originating binner (subset only)")

ggplot(binner, aes(x = bin_set, y = n, fill = arm)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
            vjust = -0.4, colour = MUTED, size = 3.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ARM_PAL, breaks = ARM_LEVELS) +
  labs(title = "Which binner's bins survive DAS Tool",
       subtitle = "Subset only (n = 22). Dataset-wide context: CONCOCT 86, MetaBAT2 63, MaxBin2 34.",
       x = NULL, y = "bins kept")
```

# 4. Taxa recovered — the metric that answers the question

More bins is not the point; **new taxa** is. This compares the *sets* of GTDB
labels recovered per arm, so a second copy of a species already recovered does
not count as a gain.

```{r taxa}
parse_tax <- function(df) {
  df %>% separate(classification,
                  into = c("domain","phylum","class","order","family","genus","species"),
                  sep = ";", fill = "right", remove = FALSE)
}

tax_new <- read_tsv(inputs$path[inputs$what == "gtdbtk new arms"], show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  separate(user_genome, into = c("tag", "sample", "bin"), sep = "__", extra = "merge") %>%
  mutate(arm = recode(tag, sf = "single-FIXED", ms = "multi")) %>%
  parse_tax()

tax_broken <- read_tsv(inputs$path[inputs$what == "gtdbtk single-BROKEN"], show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  separate(user_genome, into = c("sample", "bin"), sep = "__", extra = "merge") %>%
  semi_join(subset, by = "sample") %>%
  mutate(arm = "single-BROKEN") %>%
  parse_tax()

tax <- bind_rows(tax_new, tax_broken) %>%
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = ARM_LEVELS),
         species = if_else(species == "s__" | is.na(species), "(novel / unassigned)", species)) %>%
  left_join(select(subset, sample, subgenus, role, stratum), by = "sample")

tax %>% group_by(arm) %>%
  summarise(bins_classified = n(),
            distinct_genera = n_distinct(genus),
            distinct_species = n_distinct(species),
            novel_unassigned = sum(species == "(novel / unassigned)"), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Taxonomic breadth per arm")
```

```{r taxa-setdiff}
set_of <- function(a, level) tax %>% filter(arm == a) %>% pull(.data[[level]]) %>% unique()

setdiff_table <- map_dfr(c("genus", "species"), function(lv) {
  sf <- set_of("single-FIXED", lv); ms <- set_of("multi", lv)
  tibble(level = lv,
         in_both = length(intersect(sf, ms)),
         only_single_FIXED = length(setdiff(sf, ms)),
         only_multi = length(setdiff(ms, sf)))
})
knitr::kable(setdiff_table, caption = "Set comparison, single-FIXED vs multi (the valid comparison)")

# Name them, not just count them.
for (lv in c("genus", "species")) {
  gained <- setdiff(set_of("multi", lv), set_of("single-FIXED", lv))
  lost   <- setdiff(set_of("single-FIXED", lv), set_of("multi", lv))
  cat("\n**", lv, " gained by multi:** ",
      if (length(gained)) paste(gained, collapse = ", ") else "none", "\n", sep = "")
  cat("\n**", lv, " lost by multi:** ",
      if (length(lost)) paste(lost, collapse = ", ") else "none", "\n", sep = "")
}
```

# 5. Does multi-sample depth degrade samples that already bin well?

This decides whether rerunning all 113 samples is a good trade. The 6
*vosnesenskii* controls already produce 2–5 bins each in the existing run; if
multi-sample depth rescues failures but damages these, the trade is bad.

**Caveat on interpretation:** the controls come from a different collection
(Laguna_CA 2022) than the failure block (2020, 2600 m sites), so within the
all-vs-all they covary mostly with each other. They therefore receive a weaker
multi-sample perturbation than the failure block does, which makes "no
degradation" weaker evidence than it looks.

```{r degradation}
paired <- bins_per_sample %>%
  filter(arm %in% c("single-FIXED", "multi")) %>%
  select(sample, role, stratum, arm, n_bins) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = n_bins) %>%
  mutate(delta = multi - `single-FIXED`,
         direction = case_when(delta > 0 ~ "gained", delta < 0 ~ "lost", TRUE ~ "unchanged"))

paired %>% count(role, direction) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Change in bin count per sample, single-FIXED -> multi")

# Tier-level movement: a sample can keep its bin count while its bins get worse.
qual %>%
  filter(arm %in% c("single-FIXED", "multi")) %>%
  left_join(select(subset, sample, role), by = "sample") %>%
  count(role, arm, tier) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Tier counts by role — watch the control rows for HQ losses")
```

# 6. Within-subgenus vs cross-subgenus

Charlotte Huyghe's view is that cross-sample "noise" is not a concern and is to
some extent necessary for binning. Twenty of the 22 samples are *Pyrobombus*;
the two *rufocinctus* are *Cullumanobombus*, so this stratification tests that
on our own data rather than taking it on faith.

```{r stratum}
bins_per_sample %>%
  filter(arm %in% c("single-FIXED", "multi")) %>%
  group_by(stratum, arm) %>%
  summarise(samples = n_distinct(sample), total_bins = sum(n_bins), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = total_bins) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Bins by stratum")
```

The two *rufocinctus* samples also test a different failure mode: 5.7M and 4.7M
non-host reads yet zero bins, versus *vosnesenskii* at 1.0–1.7M that bin fine.
If multi-sample depth does not help them, the limitation is probably not depth
at all — host reads escaping the *B. impatiens* filter are the main suspect,
which the separate Kraken2 screen addresses.
